statement: Bain projects $5 trillion to $6.5 trillion of total data-center spending by 2030 and annual AI infrastructure outlays of about $1.5 trillion by 2031, adding nearly 150 gigawatts and roughly tripling global compute capacity in five years.
why: A forecast of this trajectory implies sustained upward revision of accelerator, memory and data-center orders for years, which is the core demand case for merchant GPUs.

impact.mechanism: Rising planned infrastructure outlays translate into accelerator, memory and power/cooling procurement, since the spend categories named are compute, accelerators and memory chips.

evidence.excerpt: By 2031, the firm estimates yearly outlays on AI infrastructure (data centers, computing capacity, accelerators, memory chips) could climb to '$1.5 trillion.'

confidence.basis: Forecaster projection relayed by one secondary outlet; direction of revision is clear but the level is an estimate.

entity: multi (data-center / AI infrastructure industry); Bain & Co (forecaster)
